messages:
Sarah: Heads-up: got an email asking me to approve an RBAC change via a Google Form. Subject: 'Urgent: Approve role elevation'. Link: https://forms.google.com/approve?rid=XYZ -> looks odd. Didn't click, forwarding for triage.

infosec-bot: Thanks for reporting, Sarah. Ticket created: INC-2026-984. Security team alerted.

Matt: @Sarah :eyes: can you paste full headers (Received, From, Reply-To) and a screenshot of the form page? Did anyone click?

Sarah: Didn't click. Headers pasted below:
```
From: it-admin@example-support.com
Reply-To: no-reply@forms-collector.cloud
Received: from mailserver-12.dynamic (unknown [3.120.45.88])
Subject: Urgent: Approve role elevation
```
Screenshot: https://files.redwood/screenshot1.png

Matt: The form URL resolves to google.com/forms/... but there's a redirect param to tinyurl then to forms-collector.cloud — suspicious. Kicking off sandboxing and domain blocklist check.

SandboxBot: Sandbox analysis complete for URL https://tinyurl.com/apprv-forms -> forms-collector.cloud
```
Verdict: PHISHING (high)
Indicators: JS posting credentials to hxxps://forms-collector.cloud/collect.php, external host flagged by threat intel, TLS cert mismatches.
Files: none detected.
Recommendation: block domain, disable form, rotate any exposed tokens.
```

Tom: I clicked the form earlier (before seeing Sarah's message) to see what it asked. I did NOT submit credentials but browser autofill suggested my email; I canceled. Not sure if autofill sent anything.

Elaine: I disabled the Google Form owner and removed public link. Blocked forms-collector.cloud at the edge and firewall. Rotated service account token 'sa-deploy-01' that appeared in the scraped form sample. Initiated targeted MFA reset for Tom and two others who accessed the link.

Matt: Good. Next: audit query for role/grant events in the last 24h. Run this quick gcloud query and paste results:
```
# GCP audit logs: look for iam.setIamPolicy / roles.admin
gcloud logging read "protoPayload.methodName=\"google.iam.admin.v1.SetIamPolicy\" AND timestamp>\"2023-09-01T00:00:00Z\"" --project=redwood-prod --limit=50
```

Matt: Also check KMS admin actions: CryptoKey versions, IAM changes. Tom, you said the form asked for 'KMS key admin' — can you paste that text?

Tom: Quote from form: 'Please list the service account and KMS key you need elevated to Admin so we can rotate keys and reissue secrets.' It was a freeform box.

Matt: Red flag for privilege escalation. Elaine, please check KMS logs for any CreateCryptoKey or SetIamPolicy calls from unknown IPs or from Tom's account. If any anomaly, rotate keys and create revocation timeline.

Elaine: KMS logs pulled: no CreateCryptoKey or SetIamPolicy calls from affected accounts in last 48h. There was a failed attempt to access one key from IP 54.39.21.9 at 03:12 UTC that did not authenticate. We'll schedule rotation for the key referenced in the form within 24h and enable an alert for key-privilege changes.

SecurityOps: We'll draft an org-wide note: high-level summary, do NOT click unknown external forms, how to report. Also schedule an immediate focused awareness session for Product and Infra teams. Plan phishing simulation for next week.

Matt: I'll create the incident ticket INC-2026-984-PR and kick off a post-incident writeup (blameless) with recommended actions: 1) block forms-collector.cloud org-wide, 2) add KMS IAM-change alert, 3) update phish-report playbook to include quick KMS checks, 4) run targeted phishing awareness for Product.

Sarah: Thanks all — appreciate the quick containment :thumbsup:

infosec-bot: Incident INC-2026-984 updated: containment actions recorded, postmortem assigned to Matt.

SecurityOps: Follow-ups: schedule key rotation, update runbook, and confirm users received awareness email. Will close ticket after postmortem published. :white_check_mark:
